title: How Topocode turns source into an explorable architecture site
summary: Topo scans a Git repository into a deterministic graph, generates a static site, serves an explorer, and lets you author source-grounded stories that render through a pinned viewer and bundle for plain static hosting.

sections.title: 1. Scan source into a graph
sections.body: The TypeScript scanner walks a Git repository and produces a deterministic graph of files, modules, and relationships — the raw evidence every later stage builds on.

sections.title: 2. Generate site artifacts
sections.body: The pipeline turns the scanned graph (and any ingested reports) into the site artifacts — data, layout, and modules — written under .topo/cache.

sections.title: 3. Compose and serve the explorer
sections.body: One composition contract assembles the served payload (including curated views), and a single local server binds 127.0.0.1 to serve the WebGL explorer. Bundling reuses the exact same composition.

sections.title: 4. Author a source-grounded story
sections.body: A story is authored data: it is parsed against a strict contract, then its path/symbol/pattern anchors are resolved to real source locations — broken anchors fail loudly instead of rendering misleading evidence.

sections.title: 5. Render at the pinned boundary
sections.body: A resolved story is translated to an artifact only at the @topo/diagram-core boundary, through a pinned, integrity-checked viewer — the renderer is never mutated by authored content.

sections.title: 6. Browse the story catalogue
sections.body: Every authored story plus the retained explorer are gathered, categorized, and published as one generated landing page — derived, never hand-maintained.

sections.title: 7. Bundle for static hosting
sections.body: The composed site — stories, catalogue, explorer, assets, and license notices — is emitted as deployable static files that any plain file server can host, with no topo process running.
